tables.description: Complications that spoil a plan mid-operation

result.text: A rival service has the same target under watch.
The contact fails to appear at the second meeting.
A border crossing closes without warning.
The cover identity is recognised by a former classmate.
The safehouse has been visited while you were away.
The asset demands extraction tonight, not tomorrow.
A radio frequency is jammed by an unknown party.
Local police detain someone on a trivial charge.
The weather grounds every aircraft for two days.
An ally quietly reports to the other side.
The dead drop is cleared by a stranger.
A newspaper prints a photograph of the operation's location.
The cipher key has been changed without notice.
A diplomat's reception puts the target in the same room as the team.
The payment arrives short and late.
An informant is more valuable than briefed — and more frightened.
A cover story collides with the real tenant of the flat.
A sudden strike halts rail and ferry traffic.
The briefing omitted a second objective.
A trusted handler has gone silent.
The safe-conduct paper is a forgery.
A child recognises a face from the briefing photos.
Orders arrive to abort — but the code word is wrong.

tables.description: d6 reliability grade for an asset or informant

result.text: Compromised — feeds you what the other side wants heard.
Unreliable — frightened, embellishes, needs constant reassurance.
Uncertain — accurate in small things, vague in large ones.
Reliable — consistent, cautious, rarely volunteers more than asked.
Exceptional — highly placed, accurate, and willing to take risks.
